notes: Family "others": SPICE (PSI-107) and SLICE (PSI-106), plus every record of psi-investigations.json that the other families leave out: PSI-60, PSI-62, PSI-115, PSI-117, PSI-142 (ground investigations that reuse PSI flight data), PSI-108 STDCE-1 (Fluid Physics) and PSI-181 (Materials Science). The last two are in psi-investigations.json only because their text mentions the word "combustion"; they are not combustion investigations.

Every quote was cut by script from the cached text file named in source.text_file (whitespace collapsed), so quotes keep the artefacts of the source: reference superscripts glued to words in pdftotext output (for example "exceeded4", "flames12-16"), line-break hyphens ("con- figurations"), OCR errors in the scanned 1993 SSCE report ("l.0 atm" for "1.0 atm"), and JSON punctuation in quotes taken from raw PSI records.

PDFs fetched for this family are under raw/pdf/ with the prefix PSI-106_, PSI-107_, PSI-108_, PSI-115_ or PSI-117_ (PSI file downloads, source.url is the PSI download endpoint with the file id), plus NTRS full texts 20140017780 and 20150002322. All requests succeeded on the first try.

SPICE counts differ between NASA sources and are recorded as found: the final report abstract says fifty-two smoke points, its closing remarks say 55, and its Table 1 rows add up to 52; the fact sheet says 250 tests and more than 70 smoke points; the final report and the PSI record say 526 flames. The final report gives the duct interior as 172mm x 43mm x 43mm, while the 30-day report and the SLICE final report give a 76 mm (76.2-mm) square cross-section.

SPICE fuel ranking: the final report body says sooting propensity "generally increases from propane to ethylene" while its closing remarks put ethylene below propane; the closing-remarks version is the one recorded (OTHERS finding on fuel ranking), and the 2009 propane anomaly was not reproduced in the 2012 retest.

SPICE and SLICE ran only in ISS cabin air (about 21% oxygen, about 100 kPa) in microgravity. They hold no data at elevated oxygen, reduced pressure or partial gravity; findings about exploration atmospheres from them would be extrapolation.
SLICE: the SLICE final report itself says fire safety was not the intent of the research; its fire-safety use is indirect (flame stability, soot yield, soot loading of filters, model validation).

SPICE data analysis (PSI-60): 4 findings, fewer than 5. PSI holds only the metadata record (one file); its text states objectives, approach and a hypothesis but no results, and the one publication (Dobbins et al. 2022, Combustion Science and Technology) is not on a NASA host. Findings are limited to what the record states and are marked as aims or hypothesis.

BASS flame-spread modeling (PSI-62): 4 findings, fewer than 5. PSI holds only the metadata record (one file) with objectives and approach, no results; its publications are journal papers not hosted by NASA and NTRS returned no record for the project. PSI spells the PI affiliation "New York University, Buffalo" (the e-mail domain in the record is buffalo.edu).

Cool flame transitions (PSI-142): 5 findings, all from the PSI record text (research impacts, hypothesis, approach). The only files are a data summary spreadsheet and a table of 8 data sets that point to journal figures; the measured extinction limits themselves are in journal papers not hosted by NASA.

Cool flame CFD (PSI-117): conditions.gravity is null for findings taken from the 2022 extinction slide deck because that deck never prints the gravity level; the PSI-117 record describes the model as "n-alkane droplet cool flames in microgravity" checked against ISS FLEX measurements.

Cool flame CFD (PSI-117): findings come from two slide decks in the PSI record (PSI seminar of 2026 and a 2022 symposium talk). They are model predictions checked against FLEX; slide text is terse and conditions are those printed on the slide or its figure caption. Two larger decks (30.9 MB and 9.0 MB) and the 8.1 MB dissertation were not fetched (one is over the 20 MB limit; the others were not needed).

SAME smoke simulation (PSI-115): all results are simulations of one surrogate (dibutyl phthalate) in one geometry; the report itself says the gravity effect is material- and geometry-dependent. Its statements about measured particle sizes cite earlier work (Urban et al., Liu et al.) and are marked "review or summary".

STDCE-1 (PSI-108): 2 findings, fewer than 5. It is a Fluid Physics investigation of thermocapillary flow in silicone oil with no fuel and no flame, so its sources hold no fire-safety results; it gets a record for completeness.

SSCE (Solid Surface Combustion Experiment): not a PSI investigation and not in psi-investigations.json, so psi_id is null. Its USML-1 report is archived inside PSI-108 (Reports folder, file "STDCE-1 - The Solid Surface Combustion Experiment Aboard USML-1 Mission.pdf") and gives measured flame spread rates over thin paper at 35% and 50% oxygen in quiescent microgravity, so it is recorded here with its own investigation entry. The PI is not named as such in the report (first author Robert A. Altenkirch), so pi is null. The source year 1993 is the date of the Joint L+1 Science Review printed in the text; the scanned text has OCR noise.
ISS solder study (PSI-181): 0 findings. It is a Materials Science study of solder joints; its record contains no flame, smoke or flammability result. It gets a record for completeness.

evidence_level for the SPICE and SLICE reports is "flight experiment" when the sentence reports what the flight tests showed, and "review or summary" when the report restates earlier work (LSP, Urban et al., Kent and Wagner) or general background.
earth_instinct and decision_hint are the extractor's interpretation, not NASA text.

VERIFIER: all 85 findings passed quotecheck with --refetch (85 of 85, no FAIL, no relabel needed). All 85 survive; 39 were changed (claim, conditions, evidence_level or decision_hint narrowed to the quote) and are listed with reasons in others.rejects.md. No finding was rejected outright.

VERIFIER: live re-download on 2026-11-14. Byte-identical to the cached PDF (sha256): NTRS full text 20140017780 (OTHERS-028), the nasa.gov SPICE fact sheet (OTHERS-020, OTHERS-021) and the nasa.gov SLICE fact sheet (OTHERS-042). quotecheck --refetch also found the quotes of OTHERS-030, -031, -038 and -039 in the live NTRS records. psi.nasa.gov answered 504 / 500 on every try during verification, so PSI-hosted sources (PSI-106, -107, -108, -115, -117 files and the PSI-60, -62, -142 records) could not be re-downloaded and rest on the cached copies only.

VERIFIER: the SSCE spread rates (OTHERS-077) come from pdftotext output of a scanned 1993 report with OCR noise ('l.0 atm'); each number appears once in the text and could not be cross-checked against a second NASA source or the live PDF. Display them with the source next to them.
VERIFIER: earth_instinct was outside the checks except where it was plainly unfair (OTHERS-084, set to null); it remains the extractor's interpretation, not NASA text.

VERIFIER: investigation records: psi_id and psi_url match psi-investigations.json for the nine PSI records; SSCE has psi_id null because it is not a PSI investigation. Every source quote of every record was found verbatim in its text_file; 24 fields were narrowed to their cited quotes (listed in others.rejects.md). Empty 'fuels' lists (PSI-60, STDCE-1, PSI-181) make no claim and carry no source.

findings.quote: Kent and Wagner [21] found that smoke burn out in the oxidative region of the flame ceases when the tip of a buoyant diffusion flame cools to approximately 1300 K. Urban et al. [22] found that the tip of a nonbuoyant (microgravity) flame reaches 1000 K at its smoke point.
